candidates.name: ChicagoBoothML/DATA___InsideAirBnB
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Inside Airbnb CSV data organized in per-city folders for ~30 cities: US (Austin, Boston, Chicago, LA, Nashville, New Orleans, NYC, Oakland, Portland, San Diego, San Francisco, Santa Cruz County, Seattle, Washington DC) and international (Amsterdam, Antwerp, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Brussels, London, Madrid, Melbourne, Montreal, Paris, Sydney, Toronto, Trentino, Venice, Vienna). From a Chicago Booth ML course context (repo activity pattern suggests a ~2016-2017 era single-snapshot pull per city, i.e. pre-dates our held Dec-2022+ panel). Could not confirm exact file names/dates or license from the directory listing alone (GitHub tree UI did not render fully); worth a direct clone-free API check for per-city listings.csv/reviews.csv/calendar.csv timestamps.
candidates.why_useful: Multiple cities we already hold (NYC, LA, Chicago, Austin, Nashville, New Orleans, San Diego, Paris, London, Barcelona, Sydney) plus many we don't (Boston, SF, Seattle, DC, Amsterdam, Berlin, Madrid, Melbourne, Montreal, Toronto, Vienna, Venice) at what looks like an early (pre-2023, likely 2016-17) vintage — directly targets gap #1 (historical Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023) if the snapshot date is confirmed older than our earliest (Dec 2022) coverage.
candidates.time_coverage: Likely single snapshot circa 2016-2017 (unconfirmed exact date)
candidates.last_activity: unknown (30 commits total, dates not surfaced)

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python scraper code (2013-2017, now unmaintained per the maintainer's own note) used to build Tom Slee's independent Airbnb survey archive, predating Inside Airbnb. The actual CSV data (not committed to the repo) is hosted at http://tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data as per-city zip files, each containing one CSV per 'survey' date; survey dates documented on tomslee.net span roughly 2014-2017 (e.g. NYC surveys 2015-01-19, 2015-03-17, 2015-12-16, 2016-05-31, 2016-08-04, 2016-12-15) across dozens of cities worldwide. A GitHub issue thread (datasets/core-datasets#37) confirms Slee stopped maintaining in Sep 2017 but preserved the archive at that URL.
candidates.why_useful: This is an independent, methodologically different (survey/scrape, not Inside Airbnb's pipeline) historical Airbnb listings panel reaching back to 2014-2015 — older than anything Inside Airbnb itself now serves on its CDN, and older than our held panel (Dec 2022+). Directly targets gap #1 (pre-2023 historical dumps) with an even deeper history; also relevant as a second, independent cross-check on any Inside Airbnb-based occupancy/price reconstruction.
candidates.geography: Dozens of global cities (NYC, SF, and many others per tomslee.net city list)
candidates.size_hint: Per-city zipped CSVs, unspecified total size
candidates.license: MIT (code); data terms unspecified but publicly downloadable at time of last check
candidates.last_activity: Repo inactive since ~2017 per maintainer statement

candidates.name: urbanbigdatacentre/ubdc-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized (Docker) Python application from University of Glasgow's Urban Big Data Centre that continuously scrapes Airbnb listing/calendar/review/host data for user-defined geographic areas into a PostGIS database; no data committed in-repo. 58 commits, LICENCE.txt present (type unconfirmed). Documented in a PLOS ONE paper (Enhancing our understanding of short-term rental activity: a daily scrape-based approach for Airbnb listings) describing daily scrapes since 2020 covering 30 Travel-to-Work Areas in Scotland plus 10 more UK TTWAs, June 2021-Dec 2023. The actual dataset is NOT public: researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056 states access is restricted to internal UBDC staff for non-commercial academic use only.
candidates.why_useful: A working, actively-documented (peer-reviewed) daily-calendar-scrape methodology for STR occupancy/availability reconstruction (relevant to gap #2, realised occupancy) and a template for a from-scratch calendar-based occupancy indicator, even though the underlying UK dataset itself is gated. Also directly scrapes airbnb.com, so per repo rules this is catalogued as method only and must not be run without a human ToS decision.
candidates.license: unspecified repo license; data access restricted to UBDC staff
candidates.last_activity: active research infrastructure as of the PLOS ONE 2024 publication

candidates.name: tmasjc/airbnb-market-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo ships pre-loaded listings.csv data for Berlin and Vienna (Vienna snapshots spanning roughly March-September 2017, ~1.1-1.3MB each) sourced from Inside Airbnb, plus a command-line downloader that can pull listings.csv for dozens of additional Inside Airbnb metro areas (amsterdam, antwerp, asheville, athens, austin, barcelona, boston, brussels, chicago, copenhagen, denver, and more per the tool's help text). 43 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Committed 2017-vintage Vienna/Berlin snapshots pre-date our held Dec-2022+ panel (gap #1), and the bundled multi-city downloader is a ready-made, low-effort tool for pulling Inside Airbnb's currently-live archive across many markets we don't yet hold.
candidates.geography: Vienna, Berlin committed; dozens more via downloader
candidates.time_coverage: 2017 (Vienna); download tool covers current live IA archive

candidates.name: Mcamin/Berlin-Airbnb-19-20
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Berlin Airbnb dataset for 2019-2020 (sourced from a Kaggle mirror of insideairbnb.com) including a calendar.csv with listing availability and price, plus a listings file, used for descriptive analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Fills a Berlin 2019-2020 vintage we do not explicitly hold in the 13-city / 34-market panels; useful as a cross-check city and pre-COVID/COVID-transition calendar with price, relevant to gap #1 and #2 (realised pricing).

candidates.name: jsvine/waybackpack
candidates.what_it_holds: General-purpose Python CLI to download the entire Wayback Machine (archive.org) capture history for a given URL, including listing snapshots vs. printing capture lists only. Not Airbnb-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Directly implements the 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)' method named in gap #17; could be pointed at archived insideairbnb.com/get-the-data pages or historical AirDNA market-report pages to recover CSVs/snapshots the CDN no longer serves.
candidates.license: MIT (typical for jsvine repos; not independently re-verified)

candidates.name: hartator/wayback-machine-downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby CLI to download an entire website's history from the Wayback Machine to a local directory, one file per captured path. Not Airbnb-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative implementation of the same Wayback-mirroring method as waybackpack (gap #17); could recover archived insideairbnb.com data pages or AirDNA market pages.

candidates.name: anguyen1210/insideairbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Small (3-commit, 1-star) Python tool with two scrape scripts (scrape_insideairbnb_01.py, scrape_insideairbnb_02.py) that pull specified files from the live Inside Airbnb site into a local SQLite database, plus an email-alert helper. No data committed.
candidates.why_useful: A minimal one-command puller for Inside Airbnb's currently-live archive into a queryable local DB; marginal since it only reaches the live CDN (same ~1-year window we already have), not older vintages.
candidates.time_coverage: current live Inside Airbnb archive only
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Reaches only the live CDN window we already hold

candidates.name: dingluo1205/AirbnbDataPipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline (Airflow, S3, Spark/EMR, Redshift/Athena) that pulls Inside Airbnb review and listing CSVs, partitioning outputs by month and city in S3. No data committed to the repo itself; infrastructure/orchestration code only.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable, more production-grade version of the 'pull Inside Airbnb into cloud storage on a schedule' pattern; could be adapted to build our own point-in-time vintage store of Inside Airbnb dumps going forward, but does not itself unlock any historical (pre-2023) data.
candidates.time_coverage: current live Inside Airbnb archive only

candidates.name: University of Glasgow — Airbnb raw scraped data collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Institutional research-data record (not a GitHub repo, but the companion dataset to urbanbigdatacentre/ubdc-airbnb above) describing daily Airbnb scrape data for 30 Scottish TTWAs + 10 more UK TTWAs, June 2021-Dec 2023: property characteristics, daily calendars, booking policies, host info, reviews, plus derived monthly estimates of available/occupied listings, visits, occupancy rate and income at MSOA/IZ geography. Access restricted to internal UBDC staff for non-commercial academic use; no public download.
candidates.why_useful: Documents exactly what a daily-calendar STR occupancy/income reconstruction looks like at sub-city geography (relevant to gap #2), even though we cannot pull the underlying files ourselves; worth citing as an existence proof and methodology reference, and as a reason to ask a human whether an academic-access request is worth pursuing before the pitch deadline (unlikely to clear in time).
candidates.license: University of Glasgow copyright; academic-only, gated
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying project as ubdc-airbnb code repo above

notes: Ceiling on this theme: Inside Airbnb's own CDN drops dumps older than ~1 year, and no actively-maintained GitHub repo appears to systematically mirror the FULL historical IA archive (all cities, all vintages) as committed data -- most 'inside airbnb + github' hits are one-off student analysis notebooks pinned to a single snapshot (excluded per instructions) or generic scraper/pipeline tools that only reach the current live CDN window (same coverage we already have) rather than filling the pre-2023 gap. The two genuinely pre-2023 finds are (a) ChicagoBoothML/DATA___InsideAirBnB, a 30-city committed dataset that looks like an early (~2016-17) snapshot but needs a follow-up file-level check (GitHub's tree UI did not surface file names/dates through WebFetch) to confirm exact vintage and license, and (b) Tom Slee's pre-Inside-Airbnb independent survey archive (2014-2017, code on GitHub, data on tomslee.net) which is older than anything Inside Airbnb itself now serves and methodologically independent -- flagged HIGH and worth a follow-up scout with authenticated `gh`/direct HTTP access to actually list files and confirm dates/row counts before committing time to ingest either. The NYC pre/post Local-Law-18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) gap specifically turned up nothing on GitHub; searches only found regulatory commentary, not data mirrors -- likely needs a direct Wayback Machine query (via waybackpack/wayback-machine-downloader, flagged above) against archived insideairbnb.com NYC data-page URLs from that window rather than a GitHub search. UBDC/Glasgow's daily-scrape-since-2020 project is the most rigorous occupancy-reconstruction methodology found but its actual dataset is access-gated to UBDC staff, so it is citable as method/precedent only. No Zenodo/Dataverse/HuggingFace hosting of a multi-year Inside Airbnb mirror was found despite several targeted searches. A useful next step for another scout: query GitHub code search (not web search) for filenames like 'listings.csv.gz' combined with pre-2023 date strings in path, which this web-only modality could not do directly.
